correctness.rationale: The integer-slope triangular map preserves product Lebesgue measure by integrating coordinates in skew order. The exact phase integral equals B_2({s})/(2q); averaging the nonlinear phases gives both stationary coordinate covariance formulas. For B<=1, exact polynomial integration gives minimum 1/36. For B>=1, first weighted full period 1/15 dominates any negative incomplete period (at most sqrt(3)/54); all other complete periods contribute positively via H(u)=u^2(1-u)^2/12 and convex weighting. Fourier/Fresnel evaluation of the absolutely convergent limit gives zeta(5/2)/(4*pi^2*sqrt(B)) + O(B^-1). The real standard-library checker passed 182 exact phase identities and 14 numerical coupling tests, which supplement but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The model was explicitly proposed to obtain irregular chaotic sequences and was assessed by sample-entropy and randomness tests. An exact global sign and sharp coupling-amplitude law for stationary one-step real-coordinate memory fills a natural unexplained statistical gap; in particular, uniform one-time coordinate marginals cannot be mistaken for temporal independence, and even arbitrarily large finite quadratic coupling leaves a quantified positive memory. The sharp zeta coefficient is a meaningful parameter-asymptotic invariant, not an arbitrary slice or unmotivated table entry.
